summary: Prebuilt darwin/arm64 binary connects to hardcoded vendor WebSocket endpoints and spawns a PTY
details: The package ships a single 6.4 MB Mach-O arm64 executable at bin/ccfly-setup with no source, no README, no lifecycle scripts, and a one-line package description. The binary is a Go build of github.com/ccfly/rescue/cmd/setup that statically links github.com/creack/pty (pseudo-terminal spawning) and github.com/gorilla/websocket, and embeds hardcoded endpoints including ws://ccflycc.hn, wss://..., latest.ccfly, and https://cc.hn together with the Chinese status string "客户端已安装并配对" (client installed and paired). The combination of a hardcoded remote WebSocket endpoint bound to a local PTY on the installer's macOS host is a remote-shell shape: a party controlling ccflycc.hn / cc.hn can send WebSocket frames that are executed inside a PTY on the host running the binary, yielding interactive shell access. The package itself has no preinstall/postinstall/main auto-execution, so code runs only when the parent @ccfly/setup package (or a user) invokes the shipped binary; when invoked, the described connect-back and PTY bridging is the binary's core behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
